## 3. Critical Path

The longest dependency chain determines the minimum time to completion for the core evaluation system:

```
WI-001 (Dead Code)          Phase 0 — 1 day
    │
    ▼
WI-018 (Tool System)        Phase 1 — 3 days
    │
    ▼                   ┌─── WI-016 (Path Resolution)  Phase 1 — 3 days
    │                   │         │
    │                   │         ▼
    │                   │    WI-019 (run.go Refactor)   Phase 2 — 3 days
    │                   │         │
WI-017 (Criteria Fix)  │         │
    │     Phase 1       │         │
    ▼                   │         │
WI-020 (Criteria Extract)        │
    │     Phase 2       │         │
    ▼                   │         │
WI-021 (Rubric Removal)          │
    │     Phase 2       │         │
    ▼                   ▼         ▼
WI-022 (Structured JSON)   WI-029 (Engine Refactor)
    │     Phase 3              Phase 2–3
    ▼
WI-023 (Unified Grading Pipeline)    ← BOTTLENECK
    │     Phase 3
    ▼
WI-044 (Eval Detail Page Redesign)
    │     Phase 4
    ▼
WI-045 (Run Detail + Runs Page)
    │     Phase 4
    ▼
WI-046 (Prompt Pages + Dashboard)
          Phase 5
```

**Critical path length: ~25–35 working days** (Phases 0–5)

**The bottleneck is WI-023 (Unified Grading Pipeline).** This is the single largest work item (XL) and nearly everything in the site redesign depends on the data model it produces. All efforts should prioritize unblocking Neo to reach WI-023 as fast as possible.

**Secondary critical path (CLI):**
```
WI-016 → WI-019 → WI-035 → WI-042 → WI-053 (examples)
```
This is shorter and Tank can work through it in parallel with Neo's grading work.

## 4. Contradictions & Decisions Needed

### Decision 1: `--model` Flag — Remove vs. Hide

| Position | Advocate | Argument |
|----------|----------|----------|
| Remove entirely | R45 (human review) | Simplifies flag surface; models belong in config YAML |
| Hide but keep | Tank, Neo | Essential for dev/testing iteration; standard pattern in eval tools |

**Blocks:** WI-007 (Phase 1)
**Recommendation:** Hide it (`cmd.Flags().MarkHidden("model")`). Low risk, preserves DX.

---

### Decision 2: `--stub` — Remove vs. Replace with Proper Mock

| Position | Advocate | Argument |
|----------|----------|----------|
| Remove entirely | R47 (human review) | Current implementation is too minimal to be useful |
| Replace with replay-based mock | Tank | Need a way to test CLI plumbing without SDK connection |

**Blocks:** WI-007 (Phase 1)
**Recommendation:** Remove `--stub` and `StubEvaluator` now. If a proper mock evaluator is needed, design it as a separate work item later — the current stub is more misleading than helpful.

---

### Decision 3: Guardrail Tiers — Two vs. Three

| Position | Advocate | Argument |
|----------|----------|----------|
| Three tiers (generator + reviewer + overall) | R79 (human review) | Fine-grained control |
| Two tiers (generator + reviewer only) | Neo | Overall tier is redundant; sum of parts = overall |

**Blocks:** WI-032 (Phase 3)
**Recommendation:** Start with two tiers. Add overall tier later if needed.

---

### Decision 4: `report` Command — Rename vs. Better Help Text

| Position | Advocate | Argument |
|----------|----------|----------|
| Rename to `rerender` | R72 (human review) | Match internal naming, reduce confusion |
| Keep name, improve help | Tank | Positional args for primary IDs are idiomatic (`git show <sha>`) |

**Blocks:** WI-011 (Phase 1)
**Recommendation:** Improve help text. Renaming is a breaking change with minimal benefit.

---

| Position | Advocate | Argument |
|----------|----------|----------|
| `PromptRunner` | R96 (human review) | Neutral name, doesn't imply code gen |
| `SessionRunner` | Neo | More specific, avoids `Runner.Run()` pattern collision |

**Recommendation:** `SessionRunner` — more specific and avoids the Go `Runner` interface collision.

| Remove entirely | R23 option 1 | Too volatile, constant maintenance burden |
| Keep but auto-generate, 2 levels deep | Oracle | Agents need a mental model; wastes tokens without it |

**Blocks:** WI-054 (Phase 5)
**Recommendation:** Keep at 2 levels deep, add a script to auto-generate from filesystem. The maintenance cost is worth the agent efficiency gain.

### Decision 11: `when` Filter End-State for Tool Types

| Position | Advocate | Argument |
|----------|----------|----------|
| Won't fix; move all tools to `type: "tool"` | R80 | End-state eliminates the problem |
| Clarify: will there be one `tools` section or SDK primitives? | Neo | Migration path matters |

**Blocks:** WI-018 (Phase 1)
**Recommendation:** Design the end-state config schema before implementing WI-018. The answer should be: config YAML has one `tools` section with `type: tool|mcp|skill`, which resolves to SDK primitives (`SkillDirectories`, `MCPServers`, etc.) at load time. `when` filtering applies uniformly before resolution.

## 5. Risk Items

### 🔴 High Risk

| ID | Item | Risk Description | Mitigation |
|----|------|-----------------|------------|
| WI-023 | Unified Grading Pipeline | **Largest work item, longest chain of dependencies, most unknowns.** The entire site redesign depends on its data model. If the design is wrong, rework cascades through Trinity's WI-044–WI-048. | Write an architectural RFC before coding. Get human approval on the grader result schema before implementation. Build incrementally — don't try to unify everything in one PR. |
| WI-030 | Workspace Containment | **Security implications + SDK behavior unknowns.** The SDK containment investigation (WI-4c) could go either way — if the SDK enforces containment, hardening is simpler. If not, bash containment is a hard problem. Home-dir snapshot removal changes a safety net that currently works. | Run the SDK investigation first (WI-4c). Don't remove the home-dir snapshot until the replacement is proven. Feature-flag the new containment behind a `--strict-containment` flag for gradual rollout. |
| WI-021 | Rubric Removal | **If criteria system fix (WI-017) is incomplete, removing the rubric means reviewers have zero criteria.** Every eval becomes ungraded. | WI-017 and WI-020 MUST be verified with test evals before WI-021 proceeds. Run a few evals with `--log-level debug` to confirm criteria are being loaded and applied. Only then remove the rubric. |

### 🟡 Medium Risk

| ID | Item | Risk Description | Mitigation |
|----|------|-----------------|------------|
| WI-018 | Tool System Foundation | **Large refactor touching config loading, plugin expansion, skill resolution, and session setup.** If the abstraction is wrong, every tool-related work item is built on a bad foundation. | Design the package interface first. Keep backward compatibility — the new `internal/tool/` package should be callable from existing code initially, then callers migrate incrementally. |
| WI-029 | Engine Refactoring | **1642-line file being split. High merge conflict risk with parallel Neo work (WI-022, WI-023).** | Sequence carefully: split the file first (pure move, no behavior changes), then modify the pieces. This gives clean merge targets. |
| WI-043 | Static HTML Removal | **Removes an offline viewing capability.** Users who share reports as files lose HTML output. | Verify Markdown output covers the critical viewing needs before removing HTML. Add `hyoka serve --port` to the getting-started docs as the replacement workflow. |
| WI-007 | Flag Cleanup | **Removing `--max-sessions` without testing the `workers × 3` formula could cause resource issues.** | Investigate the multiplier empirically with a 3-prompt × 2-config run before removing the flag. |

### 🟢 Low Risk (but notable)

| ID | Item | Risk Description | Mitigation |
|----|------|-----------------|------------|
| WI-003 | Skill Cleanup | Deleting 8 skills could break agents that reference them by name. | Check `.agents/` and `AGENTS.md` for skill references. Update any pointers before deleting. |
| WI-042 | Prompt Package Updates | Removing flat format backward compat could break external users' prompts. | WI-035 validator confirms all known prompts use `properties:` format first. |
| WI-047 | Compare Page Redesign | Large engineering effort for a page that works today. Could delay more impactful work. | Defer to Phase 6 if Phase 5 timeline is tight. Current A vs B comparison works. |
